slides.text:
Go has two built-in collections: a **slice**, a growable list, and a **map**, which holds values under keys.

This module shows only what the next modules need.
**Arrays** have a length that is part of their type, so `[3]int` and `[4]int` are different types. Real code uses slices almost everywhere.

exercises.title: A list of values
exercises.guide: Write a slice literal and read from it.

chunks.guide: A slice literal: the type `[]int` comes first, then the values in braces.

notes.text: A slice of ints: the type comes before the values.

chunks.guide: Index from 0, and `len` counts the elements.

exercises.title: Append returns the slice
exercises.guide: Start from an empty slice and grow it.

chunks.guide: A slice declared without a value is empty and ready to use. `len` is 0.

notes.text: No value yet: an empty slice.

chunks.guide: `append` returns the longer slice, so you store it back. It takes one value or several.

notes.text: The original slice is unchanged, so assign the result back.

exercises.title: Keep the longer slice
exercises.guide: Store the result so `queue` holds all three names.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.explanation: `append` returns a new slice and leaves `s` as it was. `s` still has 2 values and `t` has 3.

slides.text: A **map** holds values under keys. Its type names both: `map[string]int` has string keys and int values.

exercises.title: A map of values
exercises.guide: Write a map literal, read a key and add one.

chunks.guide: `map[string]int` has string keys and int values.

notes.text: Keys are strings, values are ints.

chunks.guide: `stock["tea"]` reads a key. Assigning to a key that is not there adds it.

notes.text: Assigning to a new key adds it.

chunks.guide: `Println` prints a map sorted by key, so the output is always the same.

exercises.title: A key that is not there
exercises.guide: Read a key that does not exist, then ask whether it does.

chunks.guide: A missing key is not an error: you get the zero value.
A lookup can return a second value, `true` when the key was there. By convention it is named `ok`.

notes.text: The second value says if the key exists.

chunks.guide: Look up a key that exists.
A map with three items, one per line.

notes.text: Go requires the comma after the last item too.

chunks.guide: `delete` removes a key. Deleting a key that is not there does nothing.

notes.text: No error: the key was never there.

exercises.title: Name the flag
exercises.guide: Name the value that says whether the key exists.
